login: Unthrottle cpu quota for ARC on system login This change resets the cpu quota for ARC i.e. gives it the maximum CPU quota whenever a login happens. Previously, a login and logout would just use the last CPU quota value set by Chrome for ARC. This would cause ARC boot with CL:1324972 to be extremely slow on the next login in case it was throttled right before the last logout. BUG=b:118696077 TEST=Manual testing and cheets_AuthPerf autotest. util: improve iteflash help output Some lines in 'itflash --help' output got quite long. This patch modifies the code so that the output looks as follows: vvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvv Usage: ./build/host/util/iteflash [-d] [-v <VID>] [-p <PID>] \ [-c <ccd|ftdi>] [-i <1|2>] [-s <serial>] [-u] \ [-e] [-r <file>] [-W <0|1|false|true>] [-w <file>] \ [-R base[:size]] --d[ebug] : output debug traces --e[rase] : erase all the flash content -c, --i2c-interface <ccd|ftdi> : I2C interface to use --i[interface] <1> : FTDI interface: A=1, B=2, ... --p[roduct] <0x1234> : USB product ID [-R|--range base[:size]] - allow to read or write just a slice of the file, starting at <base>:<size> bytes, or til the end of the file if <size> is not specified, expressed in hex --r[ead] <file> : read the flash content and write it into <file> --s[erial] <serialname> : USB serial string --u[nprotect] : remove flash write protect --v[endor] <0x1234> : USB vendor ID -W, --send-waveform <0|1|false|true> : Send the special waveform? gcc: allow us to force -Wno-error in builds For testing LLVM/clang nearer to ToT, it's useful if new warnings aren't fatal. This allows us to set a special environment variable to get a final say in the fatalness of warnings. Tweaking CFLAGS/CXXFLAGS isn't sufficient because we want warnings to never be fatal for these builds, and it's trivial for a single ebuild to place its own -Werror (or similar) after the user-provided CFLAGS/CXXFLAGS. This behavior is desirable for things that rely on -Werror like autotools, but not great in the case of projects like Chrome or things in platform2. More importantly, we have plans for building extra tooling on top of this support. Please see bug 914081 for more about that. BUG=chromium:903652, chromium:914081 TEST=emerged cross-gcc and built packages that should've otherwise had fatal warnings. Needed a separate hook to actually `export` the variable, naturally. Change-Id: I0bd794c9c06913410722e94b04803cdc7b461bf2 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1328150 Commit-Ready: George Burgess <gbiv@chromium.org> Tested-by: George Burgess <gbiv@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Caroline Tice <cmtice@chromium.org>

error: Print errors using Display impl I have been running into Debug-printed error messages too often and needing to look up in the source code each level of nested errors to find out from the comment on the error variant what the short name of the variant means in human terms. Worse, many errors (like the one shown below) already had error strings written but were being printed from the calling code in the less helpful Debug representation anyway. Before: [ERROR:src/main.rs:705] The architecture failed to build the vm: NoVarEmpty After: [ERROR:src/main.rs:705] The architecture failed to build the vm: /var/empty doesn't exist, can't jail devices. TEST=cargo check --all-features TEST=FEATURES=test emerge-amd64-generic crosvm Change-Id: I77122c7d6861b2d610de2fff718896918ab21e10 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1469225 Commit-Ready: David Tolnay <dtolnay@chromium.org> Tested-by: David Tolnay <dtolnay@chromium.org> Tested-by: kokoro <noreply+kokoro@google.com> Reviewed-by: Zach Reizner <zachr@chromium.org>
